paragraphs.title: Enduring Oppression and the Lord’s Deliverance

easy.explanation: Israel says, “Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth.”
easy.q: From when does Israel say they have been afflicted?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “yet they have not prevailed against me.”
easy.q: Did Israel’s enemies prevail against them?

easy.explanation: The LORD “hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked.”
easy.q: What did the righteous LORD do to the cords of the wicked?

answers: The enemies’ painful treatment of Israel
medium.explanation: The plowers’ furrows represent the suffering inflicted by Israel’s enemies.
medium.q: What does the image of plowing upon the back describe?

medium.explanation: Furrows are long grooves made by a plow; here they picture deep and prolonged suffering.
medium.q: In the KJV, what are “furrows” in “they made long their furrows”?

answers: Despite the suffering, the LORD cut the cords
The suffering caused Israel to give up
The suffering produced a great harvest
medium.explanation: The passage contrasts Israel’s severe oppression with the LORD’s deliverance.
medium.q: How are Israel’s suffering and the LORD’s action connected?

answers: Long suffering versus the enemies’ failure
challenge.explanation: Israel has suffered repeatedly, but the enemies have not prevailed, and the LORD has cut their cords.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 1–4?

answers: The affliction was prolonged and repeated
The affliction happened only at harvest time
challenge.explanation: The repetition stresses that the suffering continued over a long period.
challenge.q: What does the repeated statement “Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth” emphasize?

challenge.explanation: The righteous LORD is the one who cuts apart the cords of the wicked.
challenge.q: Who is described as acting for the benefit of the righteous?

answers: They will be confounded and turned back
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion.”
easy.q: What will happen to those who hate Zion?

easy.explanation: They are compared to grass growing on the housetops.
easy.q: What are Zion’s enemies compared to?

easy.explanation: The grass “withereth afore it groweth up.”
easy.q: What happens to the rooftop grass?

answers: It withers before it grows up
medium.explanation: The grass dries up before it can mature and produce a useful harvest.
medium.q: Why is there no harvest from the grass upon the housetops?

medium.explanation: To be turned back means to retreat or be driven away.
medium.q: What does “turned back” mean in verse 5?

answers: They begin like growth but never reach a fruitful result
medium.explanation: Like grass that withers too soon, they fail to reach a successful outcome.
medium.q: How does the comparison to rooftop grass express the defeat of Zion’s enemies?

answers: Both describe the cutting of cords
challenge.explanation: Retreat and withering grass both portray the failure of Zion’s enemies.
challenge.q: What connection exists between being confounded and turned back and the image of the grass?

answers: It withers before it grows up
challenge.explanation: It withers before it matures, so it cannot produce anything to harvest.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the grass never reaches the harvest stage?

answers: The growth never reaches a harvest
The grass grows in fertile soil
challenge.explanation: There is so little usable growth that the mower has nothing to gather.
challenge.q: What is meant by the mower not filling his hand?

paragraphs.title: The Absence of Harvest and Blessing

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Neither do they which go by say” the blessing.
easy.q: Who do not say the blessing of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The blessing, “The blessing of the LORD be upon you,” is addressed to the reapers.
easy.q: To whom would the blessing have been spoken if there were a harvest?

answers: The failure of growth and harvest
easy.explanation: The absence of a blessing highlights the lack of a worthy harvest.
easy.q: What is emphasized in the final verse?

medium.explanation: The failed rooftop grass provides no harvest for which to bless the reapers.
medium.q: Why do those who go by not bless the reapers?

answers: It describes the result of the failed harvest
It adds another description of cords
It tells how the affliction began
medium.explanation: After describing grass that withers, the verse shows that no harvest blessing follows.
medium.q: How does verse 8 relate to the verses before it?

answers: Grass withers, there is no harvest, and no blessing is given
Grass is reaped, gathered, and then withers
Mowers bless, and then the grass grows
medium.explanation: The passage presents failure in growth, harvesting, and blessing.
medium.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 6–8?

answers: There is no successful harvest worthy of blessing
The passersby do not know the reapers
The reapers have already gathered a great harvest
challenge.explanation: The missing blessing reflects the absence of a useful harvest.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the absence of the passersby’s blessing?

answers: It shows that the grass never reaches harvest and blessing
It gives it a full ear
challenge.explanation: Because there is no harvest, there are no reapers to receive the customary blessing.
challenge.q: How does the final verse strengthen the image of the rooftop grass?

answers: A blessing spoken to reapers at a successful harvest
A command for the wicked to retreat
challenge.explanation: It is the customary blessing spoken to reapers, but it is absent because the harvest has failed.
challenge.q: What does “The blessing of the LORD” mean in this context?
